sentences.text: Namaskar. With Sutra 7, we move into the domain of the mysticism of sound and language,
Vak, Svara, Nada. The commentator, Ananda Shaktipata, introduces the Sutra as follows.
In this way, having explained the attainment of the fourth state by going beyond the three
cabins in the previous Sutra, now the yogin is described how in the manifestation of all
the forms of speech, which are unhindered, the expansion of the power of the primordial
sound is always present.
Sutra 7
Vak, Chattushtayodaya, Vyama, Tata, Su, Svara, Tata, Te.
In the experience of the arising and subsiding of the four forms of speech, the original sound
of consciousness is revealed. Before coming to the purport of the Sutra, the commentator
has to give an explanation of the four forms of speech, Vak. These forms or stages in the descent
of the word of language are well known in the Shaira Shastras and their commentators and are widely
accepted in other systems of Indian philosophy. But here we find a wonderful concise summary of this important topic.
Commentary, quote,
In the beginning, the four forms of speech will be described.
Parha, a Supreme World, is manifested as contained within herself in a non-dual way of fusion, all the
composition of her names in the simile of the fluid substance contained in a peacock stick, which contains
all the colors, all the colors, all the colors, etc. of the people. Her nature is an expansion of the original
vibration of consciousness, Patanaspanda. It consists in a slight movement emerging in the wathless sky of the
Absolute, as it arises universally, unhindered. The same Bhagavad Gha, having attained the nature of the
Banyan tree, which consists of a number of inventions taught by the other, the
constructs of the other, and being undivided, carrying within her the origin of all the four
names, is like the scene of the Banyan tree. Her nature is a visionary, and hence is described as
Vashanti. The same Bhagavad Gha, having made her own the plane of the Internet, which consists of a number of
inventions, thought constructs of the nature of the permanent conceptions, and who carries within her
collection of the collection of four names, just like the Shimbika truth contains in my
list scenes, she is called Matyama, the middle one. The same Bhagavad Gha, which consists of the sound which
strikes the vocal organs, the heart, the throat, the palate, and manifests differentiation, like the words
consisting of many letters, is called Vakari, the corporeal one, who has the capacity of expressing all
manifestations of form, etc., attaining a state of expressivity. In this way, four forms of speech will descend from the
stage of universal consciousness, are manifested constantly and without any obstacle. Thus, the arising and
subsiding of the four forms of speech, whose nature has been described, these two phases correspond to
creation and dissolution. Their unfoldment in the manifest and unmanifest states is constantly radiating and flashing forth.
This original sound of consciousness, Svara, is manifested in the nature of the full expansion of the great
resonance, Maha Nada, which transcends both the unstructured, spontaneous, unstructured sound. It is revealed as the
dawning of the great sky of consciousness, transcending thought and thought-free states. It is
constantly experienced without the activity of the senses. In this way, the original sound, Svara, is manifested in all the
nine-fold forms of the ninefold forms of the emergence of the light of consciousness, in the arising of the
multitude of phonemes, from within the center of every family, in accord with the sequence of the four forms of
speech, indivisibly, without abandoning their own respective nature, as just in extreme. End of the quote.
Here, we have three levels of sound. Svara, is the vibration of consciousness, as original sound.
Mahanatha, is the mystical sound, beyond the experienced forms of sound. Anaratha, in yoga. Hatha, in all forms of music and speech.
Svara, has given a translation, which is very revealing. The four forms of speech, in their manifestation of
arising and subsiding, reveal the sound where universal I-consciousness is found. He understands Svara as the expression of
high consciousness. According to him, the sutra points at the practice of awareness of the beginning and end of any utterance,
and between the four states of path. But this requires a very subtle awareness. Good. Our consciousness must reside only in a
super consciousness state. In order to take note of the Udaya and Vyana arising and subsiding of any state.
Good. When beginning and end of all these four states appear in our awareness, then Svara, the reality of universal consciousness, is within.
When this insight is applied to practice, as can be observed in the case of an enlightened person,
every word uttered, and even every letter or name, is brought down from its transcendent source,
Paraba, up to Vakari, the spoken word. Therefore, their speech has a gravity and depth which is precisely derived from
universal I-consciousness. But it opens up for us also a practice of greater awareness when using speech,
an awareness directed at the beginning and end of any stage of thought, even any word, leading us to the ever higher
consciousness. The sutra draws light on the whole question of the unity and multiplicity of language.
language. Already contained in the three beautiful similes of Paraba,
Paraba, Shanti, and Matena. A peacock's egg, the seed of the banyan tree, in which the whole
huge trees contained in a tiny seed, and the fruit containing many seeds inside. And the understanding that
every full name contains all the four levels of Paraba, and is a manifestation of the supreme world.
This sutra, and its beautiful commentary, can also have a message from musicians, for whom every sound
can carry them and their listeners to its transcendent source, Mahanatha.
Thank you very much.
